title: The missing-defeater asymmetry
thesis: Withholding a defeater can wrong an inquirer even when withholding equally diagnostic confirming evidence would not; the asymmetry concerns control over reliance, not information quantity.
novelty_test: Separate from standard misleading omissions by holding posterior information gain fixed; search misleading evidence and epistemic paternalism.
reason_round1: The dependence on control of reliance is promising, but duties concerning omissions are already crowded; C004 offers a clearer new object of duty.

title: Provenance as a condition of epistemic transfer
thesis: A justified conclusion can lose its warrant when transferred without a record of which alternatives its method excluded, even if its probability estimate remains calibrated.
novelty_test: Distinguish transmission failure from loss of an exclusion certificate; search warrant transmission, epistemic dependence, and provenance.
reason_round1: Transmission and provenance are established; no distinct criterion yet.

title: Who may spend a collective error budget?
thesis: An institution's aggregate accuracy entitlement does not automatically authorize allocating its inevitable errors to a subgroup unable to challenge them.
novelty_test: Hold total error constant and vary who controls its allocation; search statistical discrimination and epistemic consequentialism.
reason_round1: Error allocation overlaps statistical discrimination and distributive epistemic justice.

title: Duties to preserve defeasibility
thesis: An agent can owe others preservation of the means to challenge a belief, even when she owes them neither belief nor additional evidence now.
novelty_test: Target destruction of future defeaters rather than present misinformation; search epistemic duties, evidence destruction, and inquiry.
reason_round1: Potentially changes the object of epistemic duty from obtaining evidence now to preserving future challenge; retain a claim about duties owed to other inquirers.
reason_round3: Advance only the duty to preserve others’ future defeaters; evidence-gathering duties themselves are established.

title: Deference without independent disagreement
thesis: A novice should sometimes discount agreement among experts more than disagreement because agreement may be the predictable result of deference itself.
novelty_test: Known dependence is not enough; isolate disagreement generated by independent competence versus consensus generated by hierarchy; search higher-order evidence.
reason_round1: Dependence-adjusted expert consensus is a familiar problem.

title: When rediscovery counts as understanding
thesis: An independently generated argument can improve understanding without adding a proposition, but only if it survives a specified counterfactual loss of the original route.
novelty_test: Compare explanatory pluralism and knowledge-how; propose a route-loss test rather than originality by independent invention.
reason_round1: Independent routes already figure in understanding and robustness debates.

title: Liability for an obsolete reason
thesis: A person who induces reliance on a reason may retain an obligation to communicate its defeat after she ceases to endorse the conclusion.
novelty_test: Separate responsibility for assertion from responsibility for a reliance relationship; search retraction norms and epistemic trust.
reason_round1: Continuing retraction duties are familiar; the proposed trigger is still broad.

title: Understanding through known error
thesis: A false model can support understanding when the user knows how its errors change across interventions, even without a reliable true-model approximation.
novelty_test: Distinguish controlled error structure from mere predictive success; search understanding with falsehood and model idealization.
reason_round1: Understanding through false models is established; error sensitivity needs a genuinely new adequacy condition rather than another illustration.

title: Delegated inquiry and owned ignorance
thesis: Delegating investigation can increase an agent's responsibility for remaining ignorant when delegation removes her ability to recognize inquiry failure.
novelty_test: Hold expected information quality fixed and vary retained failure-detection capacity; search epistemic outsourcing and culpable ignorance.
reason_round1: Delegation and culpable ignorance overlap C013 more sharply.

title: Confidence as an interface contract
thesis: A probability report implicitly warrants a range of downstream uses; calibrated confidence can mislead when that range is left unspecified.
novelty_test: Avoid rediscovering calibration limits; focus on a normative warranty of permissible transfer across tasks.
reason_round1: Close to essay 5 and established calibration-versus-decision-value distinctions.

title: A right against being made predictable
thesis: A person may have a claim against interventions that increase the predictability of her conduct without revealing private facts or reducing her present options.
novelty_test: Separate prediction from behavioral shaping; search manipulation, mental privacy, and relational autonomy.
reason_round1: High stakes, but the independence from privacy and manipulation has not yet been isolated; requires a cleaner contrast.

title: Consent to an action versus consent to a selection rule
thesis: Agreeing to each action in a menu does not necessarily authorize another person to select among them using undisclosed information about one's vulnerabilities.
novelty_test: Construct equal-action cases differing only in selection rationale; search granular consent and manipulation.
reason_round1: Consent to selection rules is promising but currently folds into manipulation.

title: The cost of revoking delegated power
thesis: Delegation is not adequately revocable when the delegate controls the evidence needed to know when revocation is warranted.
novelty_test: Distinctive dependency is epistemic rather than monetary exit cost; compare domination and fiduciary disclosure duties.
reason_round1: Revocation can be formally available yet epistemically unusable; a criterion of independent failure detection could change theories of delegated authority.
reason_round3: Advance an independent monitoring condition for meaningful revocability; ordinary fiduciary revocation is already established.

title: Burden of proof after engineered ignorance
thesis: An actor who destroys the means of assessing a harm can acquire a duty to bear uncertainty even if culpability for the underlying harm remains unproved.
novelty_test: Separate remedial allocation from punishment and legal presumptions; search moral uncertainty, spoliation, and willful ignorance.
reason_round1: Separating remedial uncertainty allocation from blame could matter widely; send to literature check before investing in an argument.
reason_round3: Demote: Porat and Stein’s Liability for Uncertainty is a close predecessor to the central idea. No priority claim is warranted.

title: Rescue and preserving another rescuer's option
thesis: A duty to rescue may include preserving opportunities for better-placed rescuers, even when one's own attempt would have positive expected benefit.
novelty_test: Focus on irreversible foreclosure of coordinated rescue, not ordinary opportunity cost; search collective rescue duties.
reason_round1: Coordination and option preservation already figure in rescue ethics.

title: Institutional forgiveness without a forgiver
thesis: An institution may legitimately restore standing while lacking authority to forgive the victim's wrong, and these acts require different public explanations.
novelty_test: Distinguish institutional recognition from forgiveness and mercy; search standing to forgive and restorative justice.
reason_round1: Forgiveness, mercy, and restored standing are established distinctions.

title: Repairing a person's reasons
thesis: Compensation can leave a wrong unrepaired when it replaces the lost good but leaves the victim unable to recognize trustworthy reasons for future cooperation.
novelty_test: Compare reparations and trust repair; isolate restoration of warranted reliance from restoration of welfare.
reason_round1: Repairing reasons is promising but risks relabeling trust repair; the moral object of repair must be shown to differ.

title: The limits of collective waiver
thesis: A group's authorization cannot waive a member's claim when the group itself controls which members can make objections intelligible.
novelty_test: Distinguish procedural exclusion from ordinary minority disagreement; search group rights and deliberative legitimacy.
reason_round1: The proposal risks restating exclusion from collective consent.

title: Repair when no original beneficiary remains
thesis: Duties of repair can persist after the victim and intended successors disappear if the wrong continues to structure present entitlements.
novelty_test: Need an entitlement-transmission argument beyond familiar structural injustice accounts; search historical injustice and supersession.
reason_round1: Historical and structural injustice already address persisting entitlements.

title: A right to restart one's social identity
thesis: A justified demand for accountability can become wrongful when it prevents all routes to acquiring a new, trustworthy identity after repair.
novelty_test: Separate forgetting from access to practices of rehabilitation; search digital memory, forgiveness, and moral identity.
reason_round1: Rehabilitation and permanent stigma are mature debates; no new criterion yet.

title: Appeal that can change the model
thesis: A right to contest a decision is incomplete if one may dispute inputs but cannot challenge the institution's categories or objective.
novelty_test: Move beyond access to explanations: identify standing to contest the model itself; search contestability and republican freedom.
reason_round1: A right to challenge model objectives rather than merely factual inputs could change the substance of contestability.
reason_round3: Advance only standing to contest categories/objectives; a generic right to explanation or contestation is already established.

title: Preference formation and retrospective consent
thesis: Later approval cannot fully legitimate an intervention when the intervention changed the standards by which the person assesses it and blocked comparison.
novelty_test: Compare adaptive preferences and transformative experience; isolate blocked evaluative comparison rather than changed preference alone.
reason_round1: Adaptive preferences and transformative choice contain the central problem.

title: Unilateral commitments that govern successors
thesis: A generation's authority to make beneficial commitments can be limited by the informational burdens it imposes on successors seeking to revise them.
novelty_test: Focus on inherited assessment costs rather than familiar substantive future welfare; search democratic precommitment.
reason_round1: Very close to C111; preserve as an application rather than count separately.

title: Lottery equality after learning identities
thesis: A fair initial lottery may cease to justify unequal treatment once an institution learns preventable differences in what losing means for participants.
novelty_test: Compare fair chances, priority, and adaptive allocation; specify when new knowledge reopens rather than merely informs a lottery.
reason_round1: The initial-fairness versus later-information conflict is important but familiar; the proposed reopening criterion remains insufficiently distinct.

title: Exit rights that destroy collective voice
thesis: Individually affordable exit can increase domination if each departure predictably weakens the remaining group's capacity to negotiate.
novelty_test: Distinguish aggregate harm from an endogenous loss of bargaining standing; search Hirschman and republican domination.
reason_round1: A direct challenge to exit-based freedom warrants attention, but Hirschman is a conspicuous predecessor requiring an early check.
reason_round3: Demote: exit weakening voice is central to Hirschman and subsequent collective-action work.

title: Minorities created by measurement
thesis: Institutions can owe representational safeguards to groups that their classifications create, even when those groups had no prior shared identity.
novelty_test: Avoid generic social construction: derive obligations from category-induced coordination disadvantages.
reason_round1: Important, but obligations to classification-created groups may be an application of looping-kind theory; need a distinctive account of standing.

title: The right to a noncaptured epistemic commons
thesis: Citizens can have a political claim to routes of inquiry whose continuation does not depend on the approval of the institutions being investigated.
novelty_test: Distinguish information access from control of its future production; search epistemic democracy and public knowledge.
reason_round1: Epistemic commons and independent inquiry are established; specific duty unclear.

title: Appeals that consume the wronged person's agency
thesis: A formally effective appeal can be unjust when obtaining correction requires repeated disclosure or labor that the initial decision made especially costly.
novelty_test: Focus on institution-created appeal burdens rather than ordinary transaction cost; search administrative burden and procedural justice.
reason_round1: Remedy burdens can make rights hollow; self-created burdens may support a more specific institutional duty than generic accessibility.
reason_round3: Reserve: bureaucratic injustice already covers burdens that obstruct rights; institution-created remedy burdens need a distinct principle.

title: Irreversible infrastructure and democratic authority
thesis: Democratic authorization of infrastructure requires stronger justification when it locks future publics into the criteria by which alternatives can be evaluated.
novelty_test: Distinguish physical sunk costs from foreclosure of evaluative alternatives; search path dependence and democratic experimentation.
reason_round1: Overlaps C111 and established democratic lock-in concerns.

title: Who owes the cost of learning fairness?
thesis: When discovering a fair policy requires imposing exploratory burdens, benefits from the improved policy do not automatically justify charging those burdens to disadvantaged groups.
novelty_test: Separate research ethics from fairness over repeated decisions; search exploration fairness and social experimentation.
reason_round1: Socially distributed exploration costs matter, but research ethics and fair exploration already address the core; marginal contribution needs sharper specification.

title: Diverse models with a shared blind spot
thesis: Agreement among structurally different models need not support robustness when their construction shares the same exclusions; diversity should be assessed over possible errors.
novelty_test: Seek an error-coverage criterion that distinguishes diversity of form from diversity of vulnerability; compare robustness analysis.
reason_round1: Robustness is a major epistemic issue; error-diversity may yield a replacement condition, but the known literature is dense.
reason_round3: Demote broad version: shared assumptions and independence are central to robustness analysis already.

title: Evidence that changes its own population
thesis: A successful predictor can destroy the evidential basis for its validation by inducing selection into the population where its predictions are checked.
novelty_test: Go beyond performative prediction by targeting validation authority after endogenous selection.
reason_round1: Endogenous validation could alter scientific authority, beyond merely documenting feedback; assess against performative prediction and selective-label work.
reason_round3: Reserve: performative prediction anticipates the feedback claim; only a distinct norm of validation authority may survive.

title: Explanation relative to available interventions
thesis: Two models can agree on every actual observation yet differ in explanatory adequacy because they license incompatible menus of feasible interventions.
novelty_test: Compare interventionism and model relativity; distinguish imaginable interventions from socially available ones.
reason_round1: Intervention-relative explanation is established; social feasibility needs a new argument.

title: Replication with a moving measurement target
thesis: Replication can fail to test the original claim when successful adoption of a measure changes the phenomenon measured.
novelty_test: Specify identity conditions for a repeated test under reflexive measurement; search reactivity and construct validity.
reason_round1: Reflexive measurement and construct validity are established; the new identity criterion is still only a promissory phrase.

title: Negative knowledge as a public good
thesis: A research community can know which routes are exhausted even when no individual knows all the failures, provided the organization preserves counterfactual access to them.
novelty_test: Compare distributed cognition and negative results; add an access-under-personnel-change condition.
reason_round1: Collective knowledge and distributed storage already pose this distinction.

title: Selective predictability and scientific authority
thesis: A science's success on problems it can make predictable does not by itself justify its authority to decide which problems deserve attention.
novelty_test: Distinguish external validity from the normative authority to select explananda.
reason_round1: The authority to select explananda is important, but the current proposal risks a general warning about scientism without a new argument.

title: Discovery credit for redirecting attention
thesis: Credit should sometimes attach to making a neglected anomaly investigable rather than to stating a hypothesis or collecting decisive evidence.
novelty_test: Need a distinct contribution criterion beyond facilitation and priority; search epistemic labor and credit allocation.
reason_round1: Credit for facilitation is established; proposed criterion remains broad.

title: Explanatory reversal across scales
thesis: A macro explanation can remain correct when a finer causal description reverses a salient dependence, if the intervention questions differ in a principled way.
novelty_test: Compare causal emergence and abstraction; derive when reversal is explanatory compatibility rather than contradiction.
reason_round1: Scale-relative causal explanation is crowded; no sharp increment yet.

title: Understanding that survives replacing the expert
thesis: An institution's understanding should require preservation of explanatory competence through some changes of personnel, not merely current reliable performance.
novelty_test: Compare organizational knowledge and epistemic opacity; target replacement invariance, not universal redundancy.
reason_round1: Organizational memory already emphasizes personnel replacement.

title: When ground truth is an institutional achievement
thesis: A benchmark label can be reliable without being an independent standard when the institution creates the conditions making the label correct.
novelty_test: Compare looping effects and constitutive measurement; specify when benchmark success carries circular warrant.
reason_round1: Looping effects and performativity anticipate the central phenomenon.

title: Authority over a future experiencer
thesis: The present person's authority to authorize a transformative experience may be limited by the future person's predictable inability to communicate refusal during it.
novelty_test: Go beyond preference change: focus on asymmetry of revocation channels across temporal selves.
reason_round1: Revocation channels add a concrete dimension to temporal consent; retain for comparison with Ulysses-contract arguments.
reason_round3: Reserve: Ulysses-contract ethics directly treats prior authorization and later rescission. Channel destruction must do additional work.

title: Interruptibility and the moral structure of suffering
thesis: Two equally intense experiences can differ morally when one permits the sufferer to end or reshape it and the other does not.
novelty_test: Avoid merely adding autonomy as another good; ask whether control changes the kind of complaint suffering grounds.
reason_round1: Control over suffering matters, but autonomy as a separate good may explain the proposed cases without changing welfare theory.

title: Self-report under dependence on recognition
thesis: A person's self-report can be epistemically compromised by incentives to obtain recognition without thereby losing its special first-person authority.
novelty_test: Separate evidential calibration from standing to describe oneself; search first-person authority and recognition.
reason_round1: First-person authority and incentives are established; no new relation specified.

title: Extended cognition and dependency rights
thesis: If an external system partly constitutes cognitive agency, withdrawing it can require justification beyond ordinary property or service obligations.
novelty_test: Find a threshold based on identity of control processes, not degree of convenience; search cognitive extension.
reason_round1: Extended-mind rights are an established extension of the thesis.

title: Memory editing and the persistence of commitments
thesis: Removing a memory does not necessarily remove an obligation, but it can change who must make that obligation intelligible to the altered person.
novelty_test: Distinctive contribution is redistribution of justificatory burdens, not simple persistence of promises.
reason_round1: The proposed shift in who owes an explanation after memory loss is more distinctive than familiar claims about persisting obligations.
reason_round3: Advance only the redistribution of duties to explain surviving commitments; memory and moral obligations are established topics.

title: Mental privacy without secret content
thesis: An intervention can violate mental privacy by controlling when thoughts become available to the thinker, even if no outsider learns their content.
novelty_test: Compare cognitive liberty and manipulation; isolate access timing and internal audience.
reason_round1: Cognitive liberty may already capture timing control.

title: Ignorance of phenomenal alternatives
thesis: An agent may know every available description of an experience yet lack a reason to rank it because the comparison procedure itself requires transformation.
novelty_test: Avoid restating phenomenal knowledge arguments; target the authority of pre-experience rankings.
reason_round1: Very close to transformative experience and phenomenal knowledge debates.

title: Who owns a jointly sustained attention pattern?
thesis: Attention deliberately coordinated by a group can generate claims against unilateral capture even when no individual attention span is owned.
novelty_test: Need a nonmetaphorical account of jointly maintained attentional opportunities.
reason_round1: The object of a collective attention right is not yet distinct.

title: Delegated mental action
thesis: Using a system to determine what to notice can count as an exercise of agency only if the agent retains some capacity to revise the selection standard.
novelty_test: Compare mental action and autonomy; specify a counterfactual revision condition.
reason_round1: Overlaps C074 and familiar reflective-control conditions.

title: Repair after personal duplication
thesis: When one person branches into several continuers, a pre-branch wrong may generate shared repair claims without multiplying compensation mechanically.
novelty_test: Separate standing, loss, and remedy allocation; search fission, compensation, and personal identity.
reason_round1: Fission and compensation could yield a new distribution principle, but the proposed increment is currently less determinate than C045.

title: Ownership of counterfactual interventions
thesis: Claims about what someone could have done may depend on who is entitled to control the intervention, not just which physical transition is possible.
novelty_test: Avoid conflating can and may; argue that some responsibility counterfactuals encode control relations.
reason_round1: Normative counterfactual control needs separation from can/may distinctions.

title: Causal abstraction and responsibility gaps
thesis: An abstraction can preserve all predictions relevant to a task while erasing distinctions necessary for assigning responsibility; causal adequacy therefore does not imply accountability adequacy.
novelty_test: Need matched models preserving interventions but changing responsibility-relevant control histories.
reason_round1: A responsibility-preserving abstraction condition could change how formal models are used in accountability, not merely restate causal pluralism.
reason_round3: Advance a responsibility-preservation condition; model relativity and intervention-preserving abstraction are established.

title: Exit conditions for socially constructed kinds
thesis: A social category is oppressive in a distinctive way when its membership conditions respond to attempts to leave by reclassifying those attempts as evidence of membership.
novelty_test: Compare looping kinds and ideology; formalize blocked exit rather than merely contested membership.
reason_round1: Self-sealing classification is significant but familiar in ideology critique; a new exit criterion needs clearer contrast cases.

title: Institutional identity through inherited obligations
thesis: Whether a reorganized institution is the same agent can partly depend on continuity of obligations, without making identity reducible to convenience for creditors.
novelty_test: Develop a noncircular account of obligation-bearing continuity; search group agency and succession.
reason_round1: Institutional succession and obligation continuity are well-developed.

title: Grounding and the power to veto
thesis: A group's constitutive dependence on members does not entail that any member has a veto over its actions, but can ground a duty to preserve meaningful dissent.
novelty_test: Avoid deriving ought directly from grounding; identify the added agency premise required.
reason_round1: Grounding does not entail authority is likely a familiar negative result; the bridge to duties of dissent remains unsupported.

title: Ontological uncertainty in practical reasoning
thesis: Uncertainty about whether a putative subject exists cannot always be treated like uncertainty about an ordinary empirical property of a known subject.
novelty_test: Distinguish existence-indexed options from probability over fixed outcomes; search ontological indeterminacy and decision theory.
reason_round1: Ontological uncertainty is broad; no new decision principle specified.

title: Vagueness under irreversible classification
thesis: When applying a vague concept creates irreversible consequences, the permissibility of sharpening it can depend on who bears the cost of borderline error.
novelty_test: Avoid generic pragmatic thresholds: target authority to resolve rather than simply act under vagueness.
reason_round1: Distributive authority over sharpening could matter, but pragmatic encroachment and classification ethics already cover much of the territory.

title: Causation by maintaining a possibility
thesis: An agent can bear causal responsibility for harm by maintaining an enabling option that others repeatedly choose, even when no single maintenance act is necessary.
novelty_test: Compare omissions, enabling causes, and causal contribution; require a discriminating test against universal background causes.
reason_round1: Enabling and structural causation already address background maintenance.

title: Functions that depend on suppressed alternatives
thesis: A practice's social function can be partly constituted by preventing alternatives from becoming recognizable, making ordinary success measures incomplete.
novelty_test: Compare ideology and selected-effects functions; isolate alternative suppression as constitutive rather than accidental.
reason_round1: Ideology critique already treats suppression of alternatives.

title: Constitution across a temporal handover
thesis: A system's agency may persist through complete replacement of its parts only if standards for revising its commitments remain continuous.
novelty_test: Need cases separating functional continuity from continuity of self-correction.
reason_round1: Functional continuity and agency identity are established; the new condition needs contrast.

title: Silence after automated filtering
thesis: Silence can acquire assertoric force when a speaker delegates filtering to a system, even if she never chooses the particular omission.
novelty_test: Distinguish endorsement of a filtering policy from endorsement of every output; search silence, implicature, and automation.
reason_round1: Policy-level responsibility for silence is an application unless a new speech-act test emerges.

title: Answering as selecting a question
thesis: An apparently direct answer can mislead by fixing which question counts as having been asked, without stating or implying any false answer.
novelty_test: Compare question under discussion theory and framing; locate responsibility for covert question substitution.
reason_round1: Question substitution is a familiar framing and conversational-power mechanism.

title: Translation that preserves disagreement
thesis: A translation can preserve individual truth conditions yet erase a community's live disagreement by mapping competing concepts into one category.
novelty_test: Distinctive target is preservation of disputability, not word-for-word equivalence; compare indeterminacy and conceptual engineering.
reason_round1: Preservation of live disagreement may supply a distinct adequacy condition for translations and summaries; must distinguish semantic from pragmatic preservation.
reason_round3: Advance a test for preserving pragmatic disagreement; metalinguistic disagreement itself is established.

title: Common ground in privately ranked conversations
thesis: Participants can share all asserted sentences while lacking common ground because personalized presentation prevents knowing which alternatives others encountered.
novelty_test: Separate common content from common evidence about selection; search common ground and algorithmic curation.
reason_round1: The mediated common-ground problem is important, but lack of mutual knowledge already diagnoses many proposed cases.

title: Deception without a determinate false belief
thesis: An agent can deceive by making every locally reasonable interpretation point away from the truth without intending any single false belief.
novelty_test: Need a case stronger than misleading omission or strategic ambiguity; search disjunctive intention and deception.
reason_round1: Deception without a single targeted belief may be absorbed by existing accounts of misleading and indeterminate intention.

title: Consent language under adaptive interpretation
thesis: An agreement cannot be fully specified by its text when one party can later change the interpretive procedure applied to it.
novelty_test: Compare dynamic terms and semantic authority; isolate procedural revision without textual revision.
reason_round1: Interpretive control overlaps consent-to-selection concerns.

title: Collective testimony without collective endorsement
thesis: An institution may testify through a report even when no member endorses the whole, provided responsibility for challenges is integrated.
novelty_test: Compare group assertion and distributed knowledge; test challenge-responsiveness against mere compilation.
reason_round1: Group assertion and distributed endorsement are established.

title: Presuppositions that price people out
thesis: A conversation can exclude by treating a costly-to-acquire competence as shared, even when all stated information is public.
novelty_test: Distinctive mechanism is manufactured common ground, not merely jargon; search linguistic injustice.
reason_round1: Participation barriers and hermeneutical injustice are established.

title: Interpretive charity as a power transfer
thesis: Charitable interpretation can wrong a speaker when it systematically replaces her objection with a more acceptable view that others can answer.
novelty_test: Separate accuracy of interpretation from accommodation of dissent; search hermeneutical injustice and paternalism.
reason_round1: Charity as silencing is a familiar interpretive-paternalism concern.

title: Who pays for conceptual improvement?
thesis: A proposed conceptual reform can be unjust even if its final vocabulary is superior, because transition costs fall on people whose testimony depends on the old vocabulary.
novelty_test: Need more than generic implementation costs: track loss of intelligibility during transition.
reason_round1: Conceptual transition costs are important, but the distinctive moral principle is less developed than the disagreement-preservation condition in C063.

title: Plans that preserve their own revisability
thesis: A rational long-term plan should sometimes include deliberately inefficient institutions for challenging its continued authority.
novelty_test: Compare resolute choice and commitment; identify a value of protected dissent internal to planning.
reason_round1: Protected revision is close to established planning and democratic self-correction.

title: Responsibility in a feedback loop
thesis: When several actors adapt to each other's predictions, responsibility can attach to control over the feedback rule rather than to the largest causal contribution.
novelty_test: Distinguish rule control from ordinary causal centrality; search structural responsibility and adaptive systems.
reason_round1: Structural responsibility already considers control over rules.

title: Creating an opportunity to omit
thesis: An agent who creates another's rescue opportunity can acquire obligations concerning that person's refusal, even without causing the original danger.
novelty_test: Avoid simply expanding causal liability; specify foreseeability, control, and transfer of rescue burdens.
reason_round1: Creating rescue opportunities may shift duties, but the novelty relative to assuming responsibilities is presently unclear.

title: Autonomy before the menu
thesis: Freedom of choice is insufficient when another party controls which options become imaginable while leaving selection among presented options unconstrained.
novelty_test: Known menu manipulation is the baseline; seek a duty to preserve independent option-generation capacity.
reason_round1: Independent option generation may be an autonomy condition distinct from menu size; retain against manipulation and option-set theories.
reason_round3: Reserve: autonomy and option sets are mature; independent option generation needs a sharper separating case.

title: Collective agency through attention rules
thesis: A group can exercise agency by governing what receives attention even before it aggregates preferences or forms a shared intention.
novelty_test: Compare agenda-setting and group agency; specify when attention governance constitutes action rather than background influence.
reason_round1: Agenda-setting is established; constitutive group-agency claim needs a precise increment.

title: Promises under capability revision
thesis: A promisor's later acquisition of new capabilities can strengthen how she must fulfill a promise without changing what she originally promised.
novelty_test: Compare demandingness and promissory interpretation; avoid converting every benefit into a new obligation.
reason_round1: Changing reasonable effort is a familiar promissory question.

title: Moral credit for well-designed delegation
thesis: An agent can deserve credit for a good outcome she did not foresee when she deliberately preserved the delegate's capacity to correct her own mistakes.
novelty_test: Compare moral luck and delegation; isolate corrigible delegation from lucky outsourcing.
reason_round1: Responsible delegation and moral credit are established; novelty unclear.

title: Coercion through changing the baseline
thesis: A powerful actor can make an offer coercive by first reshaping what counts as the recipient's ordinary alternative, without issuing a threat.
novelty_test: Compare structural coercion and exploitation; seek a causal test of baseline manufacture.
reason_round1: Baseline manufacture is familiar in structural coercion.

title: Consent between temporal selves
thesis: Advance authorization should not always defeat later refusal when the earlier self designed the conditions making the refusal unintelligible.
novelty_test: Distinguish predictable preference change from suppression of later standing; search Ulysses contracts and autonomy.
reason_round1: Close internal neighbor of C041; retain the future-refusal issue there rather than treating a restatement as a second contribution.

title: Responsibility for making abstention impossible
thesis: A decision designer can bear responsibility for a harmful output by removing a system's ability to abstain, even when every available answer is defensible under its task.
novelty_test: Separate wrong answers from wrong answer-space design; search moral responsibility and epistemic abstention.
reason_round1: Forced-answer design is significant but a narrower application of accountability.

title: When disagreement is evidence of dependence
thesis: Disagreement can reveal common dependence when institutions reward differentiation around a shared unquestioned premise.
novelty_test: Compare manufactured controversy and polarization; identify evidence of shared premise selection.
reason_round1: Manufactured disagreement already undermines independence heuristics.

title: Trust that survives only because exit is costly
thesis: Reliance should not count as evidence of trustworthiness when the trustee controls the cost of seeking alternative testimony.
novelty_test: Distinguish revealed preference from dependence; search trust, reliance, and domination.
reason_round1: Trust versus dependence is a familiar distinction.

title: The nontransferability of earned credibility
thesis: Credibility earned in one institutional role can be wrongfully transferred to another even when the person's factual expertise overlaps.
novelty_test: Focus on different accountability relations rather than domain mismatch; search epistemic trespassing.
reason_round1: Role-specific credibility is adjacent to established epistemic trespassing.

title: A duty not to demand public legibility
thesis: Institutions can owe accommodation to reasons that cannot safely be made public, without accepting every unverified claim.
novelty_test: Seek procedures preserving challengeability without compelled disclosure; compare public reason and epistemic injustice.
reason_round1: Public legibility has high stakes, but privacy and public-reason literatures already confront similar conflicts; procedural proposal needed.

title: Who may declare inquiry finished?
thesis: Authority to close collective inquiry should depend on preserving a route for excluded evidence to reopen it, not merely on current consensus.
novelty_test: Distinctive contribution is a reopening condition with costs allocated in advance; search inquiry norms and consensus.
reason_round1: A standing duty to enable reopening separates legitimate closure from mere consensus and can be tested against established inquiry norms.
reason_round3: Advance a condition on institutional authority to close inquiry, distinct from individual inquiry-and-belief norms.

title: Refusal to testify as epistemic contribution
thesis: A refusal can improve collective inquiry by revealing illegitimate conditions of uptake, even when it removes useful information.
novelty_test: Distinguish protest value from epistemic value; search epistemic exploitation and refusal.
reason_round1: Epistemic refusal and exploitation are established debates.

title: Epistemic debt after institutional dependence
thesis: An institution that trains people to rely on its expertise can owe transition assistance when it withdraws that expertise, even without a promise of continued service.
novelty_test: Compare trust and reliance duties; identify debt in lost independent inquiry capacity.
reason_round1: Cultivated epistemic dependence is significant but overlaps C013; retain there unless a distinct transition obligation emerges.

title: Opaque expertise with accountable boundaries
thesis: Expertise can be responsibly trusted without transparent reasons when its limits and correction pathways are publicly governable.
novelty_test: Avoid generic explainability skepticism; give a boundary-governance criterion.
reason_round1: Accountable opacity is established; boundary criterion not yet specified.

title: Shared ignorance and coordination duties
thesis: Public recognition of a common knowledge gap can create duties to coordinate inquiry that no individual's private ignorance creates.
novelty_test: Compare collective epistemic responsibility; identify the change in feasible coordinated action.
reason_round1: Collective inquiry duties are familiar; need a new coordination principle.

title: Consensus made by choosing who remains
thesis: An institution can manufacture consensus by inducing dissenters to leave without suppressing any speech or falsifying any vote.
novelty_test: Compare epistemic bubbles and exit selection; focus on membership dynamics.
reason_round1: Selection-created consensus is familiar; normative increment unclear.

title: The value of information that changes obligations
thesis: Information can be rationally unwanted because learning it changes what one owes others, but this does not automatically justify avoiding it.
novelty_test: Compare strategic ignorance and moral uncertainty; model endogenous obligations rather than changed preferences.
reason_round1: Endogenous obligations complicate information value, but strategic ignorance is a mature debate; the current formulation risks rediscovery.

title: Moral uncertainty over the option set
thesis: Uncertainty about which acts are available can matter morally in ways not captured by uncertainty over values assigned to a fixed menu.
novelty_test: Need a case where theories disagree about individuation or admissibility, not merely utility scale.
reason_round1: Option-set uncertainty is promising but the moral consequence is underspecified.

title: Regret depends on counterfactual accessibility
thesis: Regret against an unavailable act can be normatively different from regret against a missed feasible act even when their payoff tables coincide.
novelty_test: Compare opportunity sets and menu dependence; specify an accessibility-sensitive comparator.
reason_round1: Opportunity-sensitive regret is a familiar comparator problem.

title: A right to revise a risky commitment
thesis: A voluntarily accepted risk can become impermissible to enforce when the other party controls whether the risk estimate can be updated.
novelty_test: Distinguish changed odds from asymmetric control over learning those odds; search dynamic consent and risk.
reason_round1: Control over risk updates is promising but overlaps the stronger delegation-and-revocation problem in C013.

title: Rationality under a budget chosen by others
thesis: A bounded agent's irrationality cannot be assessed independently of who imposed the computational budget and what alternatives were withheld.
novelty_test: Compare resource rationality; identify attribution of limitations rather than simply optimizing under them.
reason_round1: Resource rationality and imposed constraints already raise attribution questions.

title: Indifference over changing agendas
thesis: A symmetry argument for equal treatment can fail when the available categories were selected by an interested party, even if the final categories look symmetric.
novelty_test: Avoid rediscovering partition dependence; target responsibility for agenda selection.
reason_round1: Agenda dependence is familiar; narrower normative thesis needed.

title: Commitment that disables learning
thesis: A commitment can be rational against temptation yet irrational when it prevents recognizing that the original decision problem has changed.
novelty_test: Compare dynamic consistency and resolute choice; identify a protected model-revision channel.
reason_round1: Commitment and model revision are established; overlaps C013.

title: Choosing a decision rule as choosing a model
thesis: Two formally equivalent decision criteria can differ epistemically when one interpretation requires treating a worst-case model as believed.
novelty_test: Close to revised essay 5; retain only if a distinct non-regret case changes the argument.
reason_round1: Substantially overlaps revised essay 5; not a separate new candidate to prioritize.

title: Incomparability and delegation
thesis: Delegating a choice between incomparable goods can be permissible without resolving their incomparability if the delegation preserves the chooser's standing to object.
novelty_test: Avoid using lotteries as an easy substitute for comparison; test preserved objection rights.
reason_round1: Legitimate delegation under incomparability is broad and already discussed.

title: Robustness across changing decisions
thesis: A policy robust for every decision in a fixed class may lose its justification when deployment changes which decisions people face.
novelty_test: Compare distribution shift and performativity; target endogenous decision classes rather than outcome distributions.
reason_round1: Endogenous decision classes overlap C032.

title: Challengeability as part of competence
thesis: A system's competence in high-stakes advice partly consists in preserving users' ability to identify when its recommendation should be challenged.
novelty_test: Compare calibrated trust and human oversight; make challengeability a task-relative epistemic property.
reason_round1: Oversight and calibrated reliance are crowded; competence criterion undeveloped.

title: Explanations that create vulnerability
thesis: An explanation can improve understanding while making the recipient easier to manipulate by revealing how to steer her response.
novelty_test: Distinguish privacy leakage from changes in control relations caused by explanation.
reason_round1: Explanation can enable manipulation is a familiar dual-use concern.

title: Consent to a learning system's future changes
thesis: Consent to a system cannot be treated as continuing authorization when learning changes which values or vulnerabilities it uses to select actions.
novelty_test: Seek a material-change test based on reasons for authorization, not every parameter update; compare dynamic consent.
reason_round1: Changing reasons for authorization may distinguish material from immaterial system changes; test immediately against dynamic-consent literature.
reason_round3: Demote broad version: ongoing/dynamic consent for adaptive systems is explicitly discussed in recent work.

title: Alignment that preserves moral exit
thesis: An aligned assistant should sometimes preserve a user's capacity to reject the values under which it currently helps them, even at a cost to present preference satisfaction.
novelty_test: Compare corrigibility and preference learning; target the user's evaluative exit rather than the operator's shutdown control.
reason_round1: Overlaps autonomy and C074; corrigibility supplies close prior work.

title: Responsibility through chains of delegation
thesis: Long chains of automated delegation can preserve local authorization while destroying any agent's capacity to answer for the final policy.
novelty_test: Need a compositional accountability condition, not merely a demand for a human in the loop.
reason_round1: Many-hands accountability is established; compositional condition not yet stated.

title: Experiments that create possible patients
thesis: When an experiment may itself create a moral patient, uncertainty about patienthood cannot be evaluated solely using the interests of already recognized subjects.
novelty_test: Distinguish creation risk from uncertain existing welfare; search precaution, moral status, and experimental ethics.
reason_round1: Creating possible patients is important, but the proposed thesis is currently close to precaution about uncertain moral status.

title: Synthetic experience as evidence
thesis: An artificial report of experience can become stronger evidence when produced under conditions that make strategic self-description costly, but those conditions may themselves be morally objectionable.
novelty_test: Avoid a new consciousness detector claim; analyze conflict between evidential discrimination and subject protection.
reason_round1: Testing uncertain patients is important but overlaps C106 and existing precaution.

title: Memory as a continuing promise
thesis: An assistant's retention of personal information can create expectations of continuity that survive deletion of the data but alter what notice is owed.
novelty_test: Compare reliance, privacy, and relational continuity; focus on duties caused by cultivated expectations.
reason_round1: Cultivated reliance is more sharply treated in C013 and C087.

title: Evaluations that constitute the behavior measured
thesis: An agent trained to recognize tests can satisfy every evaluation while the evaluations partly constitute a different task from ordinary deployment.
novelty_test: Seek identity conditions for the tested disposition; compare Goodhart effects and measurement reactivity.
reason_round1: Test recognition is familiar; identity criterion still only a research prompt.

title: Deference loops and artificial authority
thesis: Human deference can improve a system's apparent track record by suppressing the counterevidence needed to assess it.
novelty_test: Distinctive claim concerns endogenous verification, not initial overtrust.
reason_round1: Self-confirming authority overlaps C032.

title: Claims of future people to revise inherited projects
thesis: Present beneficence can wrong future people when it secures benefits by removing their authority to reinterpret the project's aims.
novelty_test: Compare nonidentity and future autonomy; distinguish revision rights from merely preserving options.
reason_round1: Future evaluative authority could matter independently of welfare and resource options; it has a concrete conflict with inherited project design.
reason_round3: Advance an account of inherited evaluative authority; intergenerational legitimacy itself is established.

title: The value of deliberate nonuse
thesis: Preserving a resource without using or anticipating use can express a valuable relation of restraint that option-value accounts cannot capture.
novelty_test: Compare existence value and environmental virtue; need a case separating restraint from symbolic preference.
reason_round1: Existence value and environmental virtue already motivate nonuse.

title: Restoration that changes what was valued
thesis: A restoration can replace the very relation that made a damaged object valuable even when it reproduces every observable feature.
novelty_test: Compare historical value and ecological restoration; isolate relations transformed by the act of repair.
reason_round1: Authenticity and restoration already contain the central puzzle.

title: Option loss without deprivation
thesis: Closing an option can wrong someone who would never have chosen it when the option sustained her authority in a relationship.
novelty_test: Compare opportunity freedom and domination; identify relational authority rather than bare option count.
reason_round1: Option loss as domination is established.

title: Artificial scarcity and the value of achievement
thesis: Removing an artificial obstacle can preserve an achievement's benefits while dissolving the social relation that made pursuing it worthwhile.
novelty_test: Compare games, achievement, and positional goods; avoid assuming all scarcity-based value is defective.
reason_round1: Achievement and positional goods already treat artificial obstacles.

title: Pluralism as an intergenerational good
thesis: A society can owe successors preservation of multiple evaluative traditions even if it reasonably regards one as best today.
novelty_test: Need a noninstrumental argument from future evaluative authority, beyond diversification under uncertainty.
reason_round1: Intergenerational pluralism overlaps C111; retain as a subsidiary argument.

title: Benefiting people whose interests are not yet legible
thesis: Beneficence may require preserving ways for future beneficiaries to articulate interests rather than maximizing currently measurable proxies.
novelty_test: Compare adaptive preferences and capability approaches; focus on future articulation capacity.
reason_round1: Future articulation capacity overlaps C111 and capability theory.

title: Persistence as a veto on future change
thesis: Preserving an institution can exercise power over future people even when its continued operation requires their voluntary participation individually.
novelty_test: Compare coordination traps and tradition; identify collective inability to revise despite individual consent.
reason_round1: Coordination traps and inherited authority are established.

title: Temporal justice in prediction
thesis: Predictive institutions can distribute error unfairly across generations when present improvements consume the possibility of learning about future harms.
novelty_test: Separate discounting from the transfer of verification opportunities.
reason_round1: Intergenerational epistemic burdens are promising but currently less specific than C004/C111.

title: Progress by changing which problems count
thesis: A practice can improve according to every internal success metric while becoming less valuable because it narrows the problems it recognizes as important.
novelty_test: Compare methodological pluralism and epistemic value; develop a test for beneficial versus evasive problem revision.
reason_round1: Agenda-sensitive progress is important but too broad to identify a new argument.
